MX7 Register Map

The MX7 controller exposes its configuration through a bank of memory-mapped registers. Every register is thirty-two bits wide and must be accessed with an aligned word access; byte and half-word accesses are ignored by the bus bridge and raise no error, which makes misaligned drivers fail silently. Read the timing chapter before writing control registers.

Offsets in the table below are relative to the peripheral base address, which the boot ROM publishes in the device tree. Reserved bits read as zero and must be written as zero. Writing a one to any reserved bit is undefined behaviour and may latch the block into a state that only a full power cycle clears, so drivers should mask before every write.

Access modes are given as RW for read-write, RO for read-only and W1C for write-one-to-clear. A W1C register ignores zero bits, so a driver that reads, modifies and writes back the whole word will clear every pending flag, not just the one it meant to acknowledge.

Reserved ranges

Everything from offset 0x0060 to the end of the four kilobyte window is reserved for future revisions of this block. Accesses in that range complete without error and return zero today, but a later silicon revision may decode them, so drivers must not probe there.
